name: Gedaliah
bio: Gedaliah, son of Ahikam and grandson of Shaphan, was appointed governor over the remaining people of Judah by Nebuchadnezzar after Jerusalem's fall. Army captains gathered to him at Mizpah, including Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Careah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, and Jaazaniah; Gedaliah swore to them that serving the Chaldeans in the land would go well for them. In the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, of the royal line, came with ten men and assassinated Gedaliah along with the Jews and Chaldeans with him at Mizpah, after which the people fled to Egypt in fear of Babylonian reprisal (2 Kings 25:22-26). Despite Johanan son of Kareah's warning that Ishmael son of Nethaniah was plotting to kill him, Gedaliah refused to believe it and took no precautions; Ishmael assassinated him at a banquet in Mizpah along with the Jews and Chaldean soldiers present (Jeremiah 40:13-41:3).
